mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines for 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% in a single month, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE exceeds 4.0% but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a broad-based demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Both HOUST and RSAFS decline but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as manufacturing slowdowns signal reduced corporate profits, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 4.5%, the Federal Reserve is expected to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL y/y > 4.5% but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past 3 months signals strong consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS increases for 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%), the labor market is tight, leading to wage pressures and potential inflation, which triggers a Fed tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 3.5% but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a severe economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.
